answer: Each identity anchors to one cedar plank whose grain pattern is hashed into the harbor registry as its root of trust. Before countersigning any voyage settlement, notaries re-scan the plank and match the grain hash; a plankless account fails every harbor checkpoint. A sybil wanting N puppets must buy N planks, freight each individually, and pay per-plank registration and scan fees — no bulk pricing, since grain patterns cannot be forged and duplicates flag on-chain. An honest agent registers one plank and pays once for all future voyages.
